nodes.description: Public address state variable in multiSend used as the fixed address of the token contract.
Stored TokenERC20 instance created from baseAddr and used for all token transfers and balance reads.
Public counter of airdropped tokens, incremented by 100 for each successful transfer.
Public mapping in TokenERC20 mapping address to token balance.
External token contract function that moves _value tokens from _from to _to.
Public airdrop function that loops over a supplied address array and performs external token transfers.
Payable fallback function that unconditionally reverts, rejecting plain ether transfers.
Caller-controlled address passed as the token source of transferFrom in the airdrop loop.
External call bcontract.transferFrom(msg.sender, addrs[i], 100 * 10**18) executed inside an unbounded loop.
External calls bcontract.balanceOf(addrs[i]) and addrs[i].balance used for airdrop eligibility checks.
Unchecked arithmetic distributedAmount += 100 updating the distribution counter after each transfer.
Memory array parameter of sendOutToken holding the recipient addresses supplied by the caller.
Loop counter local variable indexing the addrs array in sendOutToken.

edges.reason: Unvalidated msg.sender flows directly into the external transferFrom call as the token source, letting the caller drive token movement from their own balance.
sendOutToken iterates an unbounded loop and performs an external call to another contract on every iteration, enabling reentrancy before state updates settle.
The external call invokes TokenERC20.transferFrom, an untrusted contract entry point that can call back into multiSend during the loop.
The stored TokenERC20 instance bcontract is the target contract of the transferFrom external call.
baseAddr is used to construct the bcontract TokenERC20 instance at declaration.
sendOutToken performs external balance reads to decide whether a supplied address is eligible for the airdrop.
Balance queries invoke the external bcontract.balanceOf mapping getter on the token contract.
Caller-supplied address addrs[i] is used as the _to recipient argument of the token transfer.
addrs[i] is used both in bcontract.balanceOf and in the address.balance eligibility check.
The loop index i controls traversal and indexing of the addrs parameter array.
sendOutToken executes distributedAmount += 100 after each successful transfer, an unchecked state arithmetic update.
The state variable distributedAmount is the destination of the += 100 arithmetic operation.
msg.sender determines whose token balance is debited during the airdrop loop iteration.
The _from parameter supplies the source address consumed by TokenERC20.transferFrom.
The _to parameter supplies the destination address consumed by TokenERC20.transferFrom.
The _value parameter supplies the transferred amount consumed by TokenERC20.transferFrom.

normalization_plan.reason: The addrs array is only meaningful as the input parameter of the airdrop loop, so it is folded into sendOutToken which iterates and consumes it.
The loop counter i exists solely to drive the for-loop of sendOutToken and has no independent semantics.
The _from parameter belongs to TokenERC20.transferFrom and is absorbed into that function signature.
The _to parameter belongs to TokenERC20.transferFrom and is absorbed into that function signature.
The _value parameter belongs to TokenERC20.transferFrom and is absorbed into that function signature.
